name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
description: A large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based motion capture datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. AMASS contains 42 hours of mocap, 346 subjects, and 11451 motions.
creator: Naureen Mahmood; Nima Ghorbani; Gerard Pons-Moll; Nikolaus F. Troje; Michael J. Black
rai:dataCollection: AMASS was created by unifying 15 optical marker-based motion capture datasets into a common SMPL-based representation using MoSh++. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet; several others were obtained privately or recorded by the authors themselves (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab and SSM). The source datasets were recorded using different numbers of markers placed at different body locations, and even within a dataset the number of markers varies. For the SSM dataset used to tune and evaluate MoSh++, subjects were captured with an OptiTrack motion capture system synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper explicitly discusses missing markers due to occlusion during mocap sessions. Markers may get occluded by the body due to pose; if multiple markers of a body part are occluded simultaneously, optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses. A coefficient q is introduced to increase the pose prior weight as a function of the number of missing markers in a frame.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data are archival optical marker-based human motion capture datasets and, for SSM, synchronized mocap markers and 4D body scans. AMASS uses marker data from 15 datasets: ACCAD, BioMotion, CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, and Transitions.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors used MoSh++ to map marker data into common SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. They manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems caused by inherent mocap issues such as swapped and mislabeled markers.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To create AMASS, marker-based mocap data from different datasets with varying marker sets were converted into a unified SMPL representation using MoSh++. For SSM, the mocap system was synchronized and calibrated with a 4D scanning system. In model fitting, Stage I uses 12 randomly chosen frames from subject-specific mocap sequences to estimate shape and latent marker locations; Stage II assumes latent marker locations and body shape are constant over time and optimizes pose per frame, with temporal smoothness and soft-tissue regularization. The weight of the data term is scaled to account for varying numbers of markers across datasets.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: There is no conventional labeling task described for AMASS. Instead, MoSh++ converts sparse mocap markers into SMPL body model parameters, including shape, pose, and soft-tissue coefficients. The paper also states that due to swapped and mislabeled markers in mocap data, the authors manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper discusses quality control of converted outputs: due to inherent mocap problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers, results were manually inspected and either corrected or held out. It also evaluates reconstruction accuracy on the SSM dataset using scan-to-model distances between synchronized 3D scans and estimated meshes.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be publicly available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de. The authors state that with MoSh++ it is easy to add more data, they will continue to expand the dataset, will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by them and the community, and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Body shape and motion data from human subjects are included. The paper explicitly mentions varying body shapes and motions, over 300 subjects, and for SSM three subjects with varying body shapes. No other sensitive attributes are explicitly stated.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that AMASS enables new applications requiring large amounts of training data, is useful for animation, visualization, generating synthetic training data for computer vision tasks, and can be leveraged to train models that denoise mocap data and potentially support fully automatic marker labeling.
rai:dataBiases: The source datasets vary widely in marker sets, laboratory-specific procedures, and number of markers, making unification challenging. The paper also notes that allowing more shape variation can overfit to sparse markers. No broader demographic bias analysis is explicitly provided.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes several limitations and quality issues: source mocap datasets use varying marker sets and laboratory-specific procedures; mocap data can contain swapped, mislabeled, and occluded markers; missing markers can lead to unreliable and implausible poses; current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time; and the authors do not have ground-truth data for evaluating hand articulation accuracy. For SSM, only two of the three subjects could have 4D scan data released because they signed modeling contracts.
rai:dataUseCases: AMASS is intended for research use in machine learning, animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning and computer vision. The paper states it enables applications that require large amounts of training data. Each frame includes SMPL shape, DMPL soft-tissue coefficients, and full SMPL pose parameters including hands; users interested only in pose can ignore body shape and soft tissue deformations, and bodies can be normalized to the same shape if desired.
